questions.knowledgeNote: Definite integral of a polynomial: antiderivative first, then substitute the upper limit minus the lower limit.
questions.question: Q1. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 1 of (x^2 + 5) dx.
questions.solution: Antiderivative: x^3/3 + 5x. Evaluate: [x^3/3 + 5x]_0^1 = (1/3 + 5) - 0 = 16/3. Numeric check: 5.333333. Final value: 16/3. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).

questions.knowledgeNote: Same rule term by term; keep the arithmetic in sixths to avoid slips.
questions.question: Q2. Evaluate the definite integral from 1 to 2 of (2x^2 + 3x + 4) dx.
questions.solution: Antiderivative: 2x^3/3 + 3x^2/2 + 4x. At x = 2: 16/3 + 6 + 8 = 16/3 + 14. At x = 1: 2/3 + 3/2 + 4 = 2/3 + 11/2. Difference: (16/3 - 2/3) + (14 - 11/2) = 14/3 + 17/2 = (28 + 51)/6 = 79/6. Numeric check: 13.166667. Final value: 79/6. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).

questions.knowledgeNote: Power rule on a linear inner function: antiderivative (x+2)^3/3, no chain factor needed since d(x+2) = dx.
questions.question: Q3. Evaluate the definite integral from -1 to 2 of (x + 2)^2 dx.
questions.solution: Antiderivative: (x+2)^3/3. Evaluate: [(x+2)^3/3]_{-1}^{2} = (4^3 - 1^3)/3 = (64 - 1)/3 = 63/3 = 21. Numeric check: 21.000000. (Same as the area under the shifted parabola over a width of 3 centred at 0.5.) Final value: 21. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).

questions.knowledgeNote: The limits run backwards here, so the answer is negative: swapping limits flips the sign of a definite integral.
questions.question: Q4. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to -1 of dx/(x + 2).
questions.solution: Antiderivative: log|x+2|. Evaluate: [log|x+2|]_0^{-1} = log 1 - log 2 = -log 2 (because 1 < 2, the value is negative, consistent with integrating backwards). Numeric check: -0.693147. Equivalently integral from -1 to 0 of dx/(x+2) = log 2. Final value: -log 2 (about -0.6931). Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).

questions.knowledgeNote: Substitution u = 1 + 2x^4 with du = 8x^3 dx, and change the limits with the variable.
questions.question: Q5. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 1 of x^3 sqrt(1 + 2x^4) dx.
questions.solution: Let u = 1 + 2x^4, du = 8x^3 dx; when x = 0, u = 1; when x = 1, u = 3. The integral becomes (1/8) integral from 1 to 3 of u^(1/2) du = (1/8)(2/3)[u^(3/2)]_1^3 = (1/12)(3 sqrt 3 - 1). Numeric check: 0.349679. Final value: (3 sqrt 3 - 1)/12 (about 0.3497). Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q5; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: u = 2x^2 - 1 gives du = 4x dx, so the printed 2x dx is du/2; limits move to u(1) = 1 and u(2) = 7.
questions.question: Q6. Evaluate the definite integral from 1 to 2 of e^(2x^2 - 1) 2x dx.
questions.solution: Let u = 2x^2 - 1, du = 4x dx, so 2x dx = du/2. Limits: x = 1 gives u = 1; x = 2 gives u = 7. The integral = (1/2) integral from 1 to 7 of e^u du = (1/2)(e^7 - e). Numeric check: 546.957438. Final value: (e^7 - e)/2. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q6; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: u = a^2 + x^2 turns the integrand into (1/2)u^(-3/2) du; the antiderivative is -(a^2+x^2)^(-1/2).
questions.question: Q7. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to a of x dx/(a^2 + x^2)^(3/2).
questions.solution: Let u = a^2 + x^2, du = 2x dx. Antiderivative: -(a^2 + x^2)^(-1/2). Evaluate from 0 to a: -1/sqrt(a^2 + a^2) + 1/sqrt(a^2) = -1/(a sqrt 2) + 1/a = (1/a)(1 - 1/sqrt 2). Numeric check with a = 1: 0.292893. Final value: (1/a)(1 - 1/sqrt 2). Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q7; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Logarithmic form: the numerator is exactly the derivative of the denominator.
questions.question: Q8. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 1 of 2x dx/(x^2 + 3).
questions.solution: With u = x^2 + 3, du = 2x dx: integral = [log(x^2 + 3)]_0^1 = log 4 - log 3 = log(4/3). Numeric check: 0.287682. Final value: log(4/3). Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q8; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Power rule after u = a^2 + x^2: the antiderivative is (a^2+x^2)^(3/2)/3.
questions.question: Q9. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to a of x sqrt(a^2 + x^2) dx.
questions.solution: With u = a^2 + x^2, du = 2x dx: antiderivative (a^2 + x^2)^(3/2)/3. Evaluate: [(a^2+x^2)^(3/2)/3]_0^a = [(2a^2)^(3/2) - (a^2)^(3/2)]/3 = [2 sqrt 2 a^3 - a^3]/3 = a^3(2 sqrt 2 - 1)/3. Numeric check with a = 1: 0.609476. Final value: a^3(2 sqrt 2 - 1)/3. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).

questions.knowledgeNote: cos t is even and the interval is symmetric, so the integral is twice the integral from 0 to pi/3.
questions.question: Q10. Evaluate the definite integral from -pi/3 to pi/3 of cos t dt. (HSEB 2057).
questions.solution: Antiderivative sin t. Evaluate: [sin t]_{-pi/3}^{pi/3} = sin(pi/3) - sin(-pi/3) = 2 sin(pi/3) = 2(sqrt 3/2) = sqrt 3. Numeric check: 1.732051. Final value: sqrt 3. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).

questions.knowledgeNote: The antiderivative of sec^2 is tan - the one direct standard form in this set.
questions.question: Q11. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/4 of sec^2 theta d theta.
questions.solution: [tan theta]_0^{pi/4} = tan(pi/4) - tan 0 = 1 - 0 = 1. Numeric check: 1.000000. Final value: 1. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).

questions.knowledgeNote: Linearise the square before integrating: cos^2 u = (1 + cos 2u)/2.
questions.question: Q12. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to 1 of cos^2(pi x) dx.
questions.solution: cos^2(pi x) = (1 + cos 2 pi x)/2, so the integral = [x/2 + sin(2 pi x)/(4 pi)]_0^1 = (1/2 + 0) - 0 = 1/2. The cosine term vanishes because its period 1 fits exactly in [0,1]. Numeric check: 0.500000. Final value: 1/2. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).

questions.knowledgeNote: Linearise: sin^2 x = (1 - cos 2x)/2, then the cosine term integrates to -sin 2x/4.
questions.question: Q13. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/4 of sin^2 x dx.
questions.solution: [x/2 - sin 2x/4]_0^{pi/4} = pi/8 - sin(pi/2)/4 = pi/8 - 1/4 = (pi - 2)/8. Numeric check: 0.142699. Final value: (pi - 2)/8. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q13; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Odd power of cosine: split cos^3 = (1 - sin^2)cos and substitute u = sin x.
questions.question: Q14. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/6 of cos^3 x dx.
questions.solution: cos^3 x = (1 - sin^2 x) cos x, so the antiderivative is sin x - sin^3 x/3. Evaluate from 0 to pi/6: (1/2 - (1/2)^3/3) - 0 = 1/2 - 1/24 = 12/24 - 1/24 = 11/24. Numeric check: 0.458333. Final value: 11/24. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q14; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Same odd-power trick for sine: sin^3 = (1 - cos^2) sin, antiderivative -cos x + cos^3 x/3.
questions.question: Q15. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/2 of sin^3 x dx.
questions.solution: Antiderivative: -cos x + cos^3 x/3. At pi/2 both cosine terms vanish; at 0 the value is -1 + 1/3 = -2/3. So the integral = 0 - (-2/3) = 2/3. (Consistent with Wallis' formula integral of sin^3 over a quarter period = 2/3.) Numeric check: 0.666667. Final value: 2/3. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by the conjugate (1 - cos x): the integrand becomes cosec^2 x - cosec x cot x, whose antiderivative is tan(x/2).
questions.question: Q16. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/3 of dx/(1 + cos x).
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 - cos x): 1/(1+cos x) = (1 - cos x)/(1 - cos^2 x) = (1 - cos x)/sin^2 x = cosec^2 x - cosec x cot x. Antiderivative: -cot x + cosec x = (1 - cos x)/sin x = tan(x/2). Evaluate: tan(pi/6) - tan 0 = 1/sqrt 3. Numeric check: 0.577350. Final value: 1/sqrt 3. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.19 Exercise 19.5 Q16; book p594 = PDF p621; value verified by numeric integration (vendor/books/_verify_ex19_5.py)

questions.knowledgeNote: Use 1 - cos 2x = 2 sin^2 x, whose reciprocal integrates to -cot x/2; the descending limits make the result negative.
questions.question: Q17. Evaluate the definite integral from pi/2 to pi/6 of dx/(1 - cos 2x).
questions.solution: 1 - cos 2x = 2 sin^2 x, so the integrand is (1/2)cosec^2 x and the antiderivative is -(1/2)cot x. Evaluate from pi/2 to pi/6: -(1/2)[cot(pi/6) - cot(pi/2)] = -(1/2)[sqrt 3 - 0] = -sqrt 3/2. Numeric check: -0.866025. (The function is positive everywhere but the limits are descending, so the value is negative by definition.) Final value: -sqrt 3/2. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).

questions.knowledgeNote: Multiply by (1 + sin x): the integrand splits into sec^2 x + sec x tan x, both immediate standard forms.
questions.question: Q18. Evaluate the definite integral from 0 to pi/4 of dx/(1 - sin x). (T.U. 2051).
questions.solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by (1 + sin x): 1/(1 - sin x) = (1 + sin x)/(1 - sin^2 x) = (1 + sin x)/cos^2 x = sec^2 x + sec x tan x. Antiderivative: tan x + sec x. Evaluate: [tan x + sec x]_0^{pi/4} = (1 + sqrt 2) - (0 + 1) = sqrt 2. Numeric check: 1.414214. Final value: sqrt 2. Verified independently by composite-Simpson numeric integration (200001 nodes, agreement to 1e-8).
